links.outcome: Readability grade level of chatbot knee osteoarthritis patient-education responses versus recommended 6th-8th grade level
links.effect: Both platforms exceeded the recommended level; Fry score was 11.90 ± 1.52 for ChatGPT vs 10.70 ± 1.62 for Gemini (p = 0.003).
links.quote: ChatGPT produced higher Fry Readability Formula scores (11.90 ± 1.52 vs 10.70 ± 1.62; p = 0.003), the only readability difference to survive correction; both platforms produced text well above the recommended sixth-to-eighth-grade reading level for patient education.

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates and compares the accuracy, safety, and readability of responses from ChatGPT (GPT-4o) and Gemini (Gemini 1.5 Pro) on knee osteoarthritis patient education queries using expert ratings and readability metrics, but it does not test a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
